claims.claim: Propranolol, a lipophilic basic amine with substantial first-pass extraction, had absolute oral bioavailability of 27.2 percent in fasting normal subjects, above the 20 percent threshold.
Metoprolol, a structurally similar aryloxypropanolamine base, showed systemic availability of 84 percent in cirrhotic patients.
Diphenhydramine, a basic benzhydryl amine, showed systemic availability of 0.69 after oral dosing in fasted healthy volunteers.
Verapamil, a basic dimethoxyphenyl amine, showed absolute oral bioavailability of 30 to 52 percent in cirrhosis, still above the threshold.
Every L1 context reports oral bioavailability above 20 percent, so no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports a low prediction for this compound class.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule.

L2 records are not yet available to test the same parent-condition contexts.
content.decision_summary: All ten L1 contexts report absolute oral bioavailability between 27 and 95 percent for lipophilic basic amines structurally similar to the query. The lowest value, propranolol at 27.2 percent in fasting subjects, still exceeds the 20 percent threshold. The query's low neutral fraction is a permeability caveat but not affirmative evidence of F below 20 percent. Therefore F at or above 20 percent is better supported, with moderate confidence due to analog-based transfer.
